findings.evidence: `typeBQuadraticEquiv_typeBShortCorootGenerator` = `(2 : K) • P.diagonalBivector b i` (line 298); `typeBQuadraticEquiv_typeBLongCorootGenerator` = `P.diagonalBivector b i - P.diagonalBivector b j` (line 313).
findings.fix: Restrict both sentences to the root vectors: say the *short* coroot is twice a diagonal bivector (integrality from `2 × (±1/2)`) while the long coroot is a difference of two diagonal bivectors (integrality from the difference of two half-integral weights).
findings.issue: "The reason is that a coroot is *twice* a diagonal bivector" is false for the long coroot: `typeBQuadraticEquiv_typeBLongCorootGenerator` (line 313) proves it equals `diagonalBivector b i - diagonalBivector b j`, not twice anything. Line 22's "Every one of them is a single Clifford bivector", immediately after naming the "root and coroot matrices", has the same defect — the coroots are `2 •` and a difference of bivectors.

findings.evidence: `ι_mul_ι_eq_bivector_add` (line 88): `ι Q a * ι Q b = bivector Q a b + (⅟(2:R)) • algebraMap R _ (QuadraticMap.polar Q a b)`.
findings.fix: Write "is `⅟2` times the polar form" (or "is the algebra map of `⅟2 • polar Q a b`").
findings.issue: `bivector_of_isOrtho`'s docstring says "The scalar symmetric part of `ι a * ι b` is the polar form of the two vectors"; it is *half* the polar form, `⅟2 • algebraMap (polar Q a b)`. In a file whose stated point is that the `⅟2` normalization is forced, the off-by-two claim is misleading.

summary: Declaration docstrings are largely accurate, but the new file's module docstring generalizes a coroot fact that is false for the long coroot and claims a divided-power result the file does not prove, and the Spin/IntegralLattice.lean overview is now stale in two places. One new Clifford docstring misstates the symmetric part by a factor of two.
